text: Fill in the missing terms about DNA replication.
questions: Replication is *semiconservative*, meaning each daughter molecule keeps one parental strand and gains one new strand.
At the fork, *helicase* unwinds the double helix while single-strand binding proteins stabilise the exposed strands.
The lagging strand is built in short *Okazaki* fragments, each requiring its own RNA primer.
After primers are removed and gaps filled, DNA *ligase* seals the remaining nicks between fragments.
Eukaryotic chromosomes shorten with each division unless *telomerase* adds repeat sequences to the ends.

overallFeedback.feedback: Semiconservative replication gives each daughter DNA molecule one parental strand and one newly synthesised strand; helicase opens the fork; Okazaki fragments arise because polymerase can only build 5′→3′; ligase joins the fragments into a continuous strand; polymerase proofreading and mismatch repair help correct copying errors; and telomerase helps maintain chromosome ends, and its reactivation in many cancers supports sustained proliferation.
